svg.aria-label: Diagram: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams now supports queues, powered by Amazon SQS, available for streams in On-demand capacity mode and listed in 31 Regions at launch with no GovCloud or China Regions. A queue delivers records from an On-demand stream to a queue consumer and tracks the delivery state of each record, so the consumer does not manage shards, leases or checkpoints. The trade is explicit. Each shard is read by one stream consumer instance at a time, which preserves the order of the records in that shard but caps parallelism at the shard count. Queue consumer instances do not lease shards: each one receives the next visible record, so you add instances to process more records in parallel without resharding, and in exchange the queue delivers each record at least once, redelivers any record not acknowledged before its visibility timeout expires, can in rare cases deliver a record again after acknowledgement, and does not necessarily deliver records in the order producers wrote them. The documentation instructs you to design queue consumers to be idempotent. A queue does not return the sequence number, because a sequence number identifies a record's position within its shard and a queue consumer is decoupled from shards, so any code that correlates or deduplicates on sequence number has nothing to use. The API shape is ReceiveQueueRecords returning up to ten records at a time and AcknowledgeQueueRecords acknowledging up to ten per call, with acknowledgement per record rather than per batch position. Dead-letter handling is built into every queue, with MaxReceiveCount settable from one to one thousand, after which a record moves to the dead-letter state and stops being delivered on the normal receive path. The critical limit is that a queue can deliver a record only while the stream still retains it, so a record that is never acknowledged, including a dead-letter record, expires when the stream's retention period ends for that record, which means the dead-letter state is a flag rather than a durable holding area and the investigation window is counted from the write rather than from the failure. A second limit is that a queue counts as one registered consumer and shares the stream's registered consumer limit with enhanced fan-out consumers. The documented decision rule is stateful processing through a stream consumer when processing one record depends on the records before it, and stateless processing through a queue when each record can be handled independently. Cost framing from the announcement is processing costs reduced by up to 43 percent versus the Kinesis Client Library, which creates three DynamoDB tables per application for lease and checkpoint metadata that a queue removes.
svg.title: A queue removes the shard as the unit of consumption, and both of its guarantees
svg.text: The shard capped your parallelism and guaranteed your order. Both go together.
“A queue also does not necessarily deliver records in the order that producers wrote them to the stream.”
STREAM CONSUMER — LEASES A SHARD
“Each shard is read by one stream consumer
instance at a time, which preserves the order of
the records in that shard.”
Sequence numbers. Leases. Checkpoints.
Parallelism capped at the shard count.
QUEUE CONSUMER — RECEIVES A RECORD
“Queue consumer instances do not lease shards:
each one receives the next visible record, so you
add instances … without resharding.”
No order. No sequence number. At least once.
“Design your queue consumer to be idempotent.”
The entity test, not the domain test
“Order fulfillment” is listed as stateless — fulfilling one order independently of others. But created, paid,
shipped for ONE order is stateful, and a queue may hand you those three in any sequence.
The dead-letter state is a flag, not a destination
“a record that is never acknowledged, including a dead-letter record, expires when the stream’s retention
period ends for that record.”
So the window to investigate a poison record runs from the WRITE, not from the failure. Unlike SQS, nothing
waits for you. MaxReceiveCount of 1 to 1,000 decides how much of that window retries consume.
THE LIMIT A FAN-OUT ESTATE WILL HIT
“A queue counts as one registered consumer and
shares the stream’s registered consumer limit with
enhanced fan-out consumers.”
WHERE THE 43% COMES FROM
KCL “creates three tables per application” in
DynamoDB for leases and checkpoints. A queue
tracks delivery state for you, so that layer goes.
Also: On-demand capacity mode only · ReceiveQueueRecords and AcknowledgeQueueRecords work 10 at a time,
per record rather than per batch position · 31 Regions at launch, with no GovCloud and no China.
Acknowledgement is not a guarantee: “in rare cases it can deliver a record again after you acknowledge it.”
Idempotency is the price of admission, and the sequence number you used to dedupe on is no longer returned.
